materials.title_en: Don't Throw It Away — Fix It
materials.summary_zh: 一篇社区报道：小区里的“修理咖啡馆”每月开一次，志愿者免费帮居民修东西。（虚构报道）

segments.en: On the first Saturday of every month, the community centre on Elm Road turns into a repair café.
segments.zh: 每个月的第一个周六，榆树路的社区中心都会变成一家“修理咖啡馆”。

segments.en: Local people bring broken things, such as lamps, toasters, bikes and torn jackets.
segments.zh: 附近的居民把坏了的东西带来，比如台灯、烤面包机、自行车和破了的夹克。

segments.en: Volunteers with useful skills try to fix them for free, while visitors drink tea and wait.
segments.zh: 有一技之长的志愿者免费帮忙修理，来访的人一边喝茶一边等。

segments.en: The café started two years ago, when a retired engineer called Peter Hall noticed how much his neighbours threw away.
segments.zh: 这家咖啡馆两年前开办。当时，一位名叫 Peter Hall 的退休工程师注意到邻居们扔掉的东西实在太多了。

segments.en: "Most things only need a small repair," he says. "However, people think it's easier to buy something new."
segments.zh: “大多数东西只需要小修一下，”他说，“可是人们觉得买个新的更省事。”

segments.en: Last year the volunteers repaired more than six hundred items, and about seventy percent of them worked again.
segments.zh: 去年，志愿者修了六百多件东西，其中大约七成修好后又能用了。

segments.en: Visitors are also encouraged to watch and learn, so next time they can do the repair themselves.
segments.zh: 来访的人也被鼓励在旁边看、跟着学，这样下次就能自己修了。

segments.en: Although the repairs are free, many people leave a small donation to pay for tools and spare parts.
segments.zh: 虽然修理是免费的，很多人还是会留下一点捐款，用来买工具和零件。

segments.en: Not everything can be saved, of course, and some modern devices are almost impossible to open.
segments.zh: 当然，并不是所有东西都能修好，有些新式电子设备几乎打不开。

segments.en: Still, Peter believes the café does more than fix objects: "People talk, share skills and make friends here."
segments.zh: 不过，Peter 认为咖啡馆的意义不止是修东西：“人们在这里聊天、分享手艺、交朋友。”

glossary.zh: 撕破的（tear 的过去分词）

glossary.note_zh: threw 是 throw 的过去式。

glossary.zh: 被鼓励（encourage 的过去分词）
glossary.note_zh: be encouraged to do = 被鼓励做某事

materials.summary_zh: 一篇个人博客：作者四十岁开始学西班牙语，讲她遇到的困难、找到的办法，以及她对“年纪大了学不好”的看法。（虚构博客）

segments.en: When I turned forty, I decided to learn Spanish, and many friends told me it was too late.
segments.zh: 四十岁那年，我决定学西班牙语，很多朋友都说我太晚了。

segments.en: In my opinion, they were wrong, although the first months were harder than I expected.
segments.zh: 在我看来他们错了，尽管头几个月比我想象的难。

segments.en: My memory isn't as quick as it was at school, so new words disappeared from my head overnight.
segments.zh: 我的记性没有上学时那么好，新单词过一夜就忘了。

segments.en: However, I soon found that adults have some advantages too.
segments.zh: 不过，我很快发现成年人也有一些优势。

segments.en: For example, I know exactly why I'm learning, and I can plan my time much better than a teenager.
segments.zh: 比如，我很清楚自己为什么学，安排时间的能力也比青少年强得多。

segments.en: I also stopped trying to learn everything at once.
segments.zh: 我也不再试图一下子什么都学。

segments.en: Instead, I study for twenty minutes every morning and review old words before I learn new ones.
segments.zh: 相反，我每天早上学二十分钟，学新单词之前先复习旧的。

segments.en: The biggest change came when I started speaking, even though I made lots of mistakes.
segments.zh: 最大的变化发生在我开始开口说的时候，尽管我犯了很多错。

segments.en: A teacher told me that if I waited until I was perfect, I would never speak at all.
segments.zh: 一位老师对我说，要是等到完美再开口，我就永远不会开口了。

segments.en: Two years later, I can chat with my neighbours in Valencia and follow most of the news.
segments.zh: 两年后，我能和瓦伦西亚的邻居聊天，也能听懂大部分新闻了。

segments.en: So, is it too late at forty? I don't think so, but you need patience and a plan.
segments.zh: 那么，四十岁学太晚吗？我不这么认为，不过你需要耐心和计划。

glossary.zh: 预料；预想（expect 的过去式）

materials.title_en: Your First Week at a New Job
materials.summary_zh: 一档职场播客：主持人请一位人事经理谈谈入职第一周该注意什么。（虚构节目）

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Welcome back to Work Talk. Today Grace, an HR manager, is here with advice for your first week in a new job.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到《职场谈》。今天人事经理 Grace 来给大家讲讲新工作第一周的建议。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: Thanks for having me. My first tip is simple: arrive a little early, especially on the first day.
segments.zh: 谢谢邀请。我的第一条建议很简单：早点到，尤其是第一天。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Why does that matter so much?
segments.zh: 这为什么那么重要？

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: If you arrive early, you'll have time to find the right office and calm down before you meet everyone.
segments.zh: 早点到的话，你有时间找到办公室，见大家之前也能平静下来。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: What about all the new names? I always forget them.
segments.zh: 那么多新名字怎么办？我总是记不住。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: Most people do. Write them down with a short note, for example 'Tom, design, loves cycling'.
segments.zh: 大多数人都记不住。把名字写下来，加一句简短的备注，比如“Tom，设计部，喜欢骑车”。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: And don't be afraid to ask questions. Nobody expects you to know everything in week one.
segments.zh: 还有，别怕提问。没人指望你第一周就什么都懂。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: But some people worry that questions make them look weak.
segments.zh: 可有些人担心提问会显得自己能力不够。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: Actually, it's the opposite. Unless you ask, your manager won't know where you need help.
segments.zh: 其实恰恰相反。你不问，经理就不知道你哪里需要帮助。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Any advice about lunch? That can feel awkward.
segments.zh: 午饭方面有什么建议吗？那有时挺尴尬的。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: If someone invites you, say yes, even if you're busy. Lunch is where you really get to know the team.
segments.zh: 要是有人邀请你，即使忙也答应。午饭才是真正了解团队的时候。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Great tips. Thanks, Grace.
segments.zh: 很棒的建议。谢谢你，Grace。

glossary.zh: 人力资源经理；人事经理

glossary.note_zh: write something down = 写下来、记下来
be afraid to do = 不敢做

materials.summary_zh: 两位邻居讨论小区门口要修的自行车道：一个支持，一个担心停车问题，最后找到了共同点。（虚构对话）

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: Did you read the letter from the council? They want to build a bike lane on our street.
segments.zh: 你看到市政府的信了吗？他们想在我们这条街上修自行车道。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Yes, and I think it's a great idea. I cycle to work, and the traffic here is really dangerous.
segments.zh: 看到了，我觉得这主意很好。我骑车上班，这里的交通真的很危险。

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: I see your point. But they're going to remove twenty parking spaces.
segments.zh: 我明白你的意思。可他们要拆掉二十个停车位。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: That's true. Where will people park, then?
segments.zh: 这倒是。那大家停在哪儿呢？

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: Exactly. My mum visits every weekend, and she can't walk far.
segments.zh: 就是啊。我妈每个周末都来，她走不了远路。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Although parking will be harder, I think fewer people will need cars if cycling feels safe.
segments.zh: 虽然停车会更难，但我觉得如果骑车让人觉得安全，需要开车的人就会变少。

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: Maybe in the long term. However, that won't help my mum next month.
segments.zh: 长远来看也许吧。不过这对我妈下个月来没什么帮助。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Fair point. What if we asked the council for a few spaces for older and disabled drivers?
segments.zh: 有道理。要是我们请市政府留几个给老年人和残障司机的车位呢？

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: That would solve my main problem. I'd support the lane if they did that.
segments.zh: 那就解决了我最大的问题。要是他们这么做，我就支持修车道。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Great. Let's write to them together this week.
segments.zh: 太好了。我们这周一起给他们写信吧。
